selection_rationale: Top-ranked druggable hub overall (degree 51, composite rank 5) and the statistically strongest axis in the network (PI3K/AKT Signaling in Cancer, 34/132 entities, FDR=1.1e-14). 7,688 compounds, 4 approved drugs.

pathway_axis: RTK–PI3K/RAS-MAPK axis (Reactome: Signaling by EGFR in Cancer FDR=3.4e-4; Constitutive Signaling by EGFRvIII FDR=6.3e-5)
selection_rationale: Highest-degree druggable RTK hub (degree 44, composite rank 7); EGFR amplification/EGFRvIII is the canonical classical-GBM lesion and Reactome flags EGFRvIII constitutive signalling inside module M1. Largest labelled chemical space of the panel (11,158 compounds) and 20 approved drugs for positive controls.

pathway_axis: IDH-mutant 2-hydroxyglutarate metabolic axis (module M3; axis from gene-level OT/CIViC evidence, no module-level metabolic Reactome term at FDR<0.05)
selection_rationale: Molecularly defining lesion of WHO grade 2-3 IDH-mutant glioma and the highest-scoring CIViC-evidenced gene in the seed set (17 evidence items, OT score 0.842); inhibitor chemistry is mature (4,300 compounds; ivosidenib, olutasidenib approved). Adds a non-kinase, metabolic-enzyme target that forces the graph models to generalise beyond ATP-site chemotypes.

pathway_axis: RTK–PDGF axis (Reactome: Signaling by PDGFR in disease FDR=1.0e-7; Signaling by PDGF FDR=2.1e-5)
selection_rationale: Proneural-GBM amplification target and second RTK arm of module M1 (degree 22, rank 31); keeps the panel able to learn RTK selectivity rather than a single-receptor signature. 937 compounds, 4 approved drugs.

pathway_axis: VEGF/angiogenesis axis (Reactome: VEGFA-VEGFR2 Pathway FDR=1.5e-3; GO-BP angiogenesis FDR=2.2e-2)
selection_rationale: Sole representative of the VEGF/angiogenesis axis, which is enriched in module M1 and is the therapeutic rationale for anti-angiogenic therapy in GBM. Very dense labels (10,610 compounds) support multi-task transfer; 4 approved drugs.

selection_rationale: Represents the third canonical GBM core pathway (CDKN2A deletion - RB1 inactivation); CNS-penetrant CDK4/6 inhibitors (abemaciclib) are in glioma trials. Lower centrality (degree 9, rank 134) accepted deliberately for axis coverage; 838 compounds, 5 approved drugs.
